covenant_status_alert.summary: FCCR breached its 1.2000x minimum at the last TWO consecutive quarterly Test Dates: 2026-03-31 (corrected TTM FCCR 1.0338x) and 2026-06-30 (corrected TTM FCCR 0.9192x). Both are recorded as 'BREACH - WAIVED' -- NOT cured -- under the Executed Temporary Limited Waiver, which covers only those two dates and EXPIRED 2026-06-30. As of this extraction (2026-09-15), NO waiver or other executed relief covers the next Test Date, 2026-09-30 (~15 days away). FCCR has declined every quarter since the First Amendment's amortization step-up (0.20% -> 2.00%/month, effective the October 2025 payment) mechanically inflated the Fixed Charges denominator; TTM Covenant EBITDA has been broadly stable-to-growing over the same window, so the deterioration is a mechanical, amendment-driven denominator effect, not (so far) an EBITDA collapse. Absent new executed relief or a material improvement in TTM Fixed Charges/EBITDA before 2026-09-30, an FCCR test at that date computed on the same trend would be an uncovered, unwaived breach. See the 'min_fccr' covenant's own 'waiver_status' block for the full detail and cert-by-cert figures.

The executed documents made available do not carry a separate itemized EBITDA add-back definition (no add-back/adjustments clause appears anywhere in original_agreement.pdf, amendment_1.pdf, or waiver_1.pdf).

EBITDA.note: Verified at three independent points that the borrower's own 'Reported EBITDA' line ties EXACTLY to the certified 'Covenant EBITDA' used in every quarterly Covenant_Calculation TTM Build with zero addback: March 2026 both 2,618,535.91; June 2026 both 2,696,995.08; May 2026 both 2,588,973.90. No deemed EBITDA schedule anywhere in the agreement -- full-text sweep of all three executed documents for 'deemed', 'stipulated', and 'agreed EBITDA' returns no hits. NOTE (ambiguity, see step 7): the 2025-Q1 Covenant_Calculation.xlsx TTM Build spans 2024-04 through 2025-03 -- nine of those twelve months (2024-04 through 2024-12) predate the facility's 2025-01-15 Closing Date, and five of those nine months (2024-04 through 2024-08) predate even the borrower's earliest monthly reporting-package folder (Archive/2024-09). agreement_ref.quote: FCCR equals trailing-twelve-month Covenant EBITDA divided by trailing-twelve-month cash interest, required principal, and lease payments.

Fixed_Charges.note: Three components exactly as the agreement's own FCCR formula lists them. (1) 'Cash Interest Expense' and (2) 'Scheduled Debt Principal Payments' are the covenant-support rows build-monitoring-model populates from debt-service-schedule.json -- the facility's own CONTRACTUAL cash interest and scheduled amortization, per Method step 3b, not booked ledger interest. (3) 'Lease payments' is the borrower's own native Cash-Flow-tab line (present and consistent in every Archive month and the June 2026 package checked; not a debt-service item). 'Required principal' means SCHEDULED amortization only. AMBIGUITY flagged for step 7: for THIS borrower specifically, the native 'Cash interest' and 'Required principal' Cash-Flow-tab lines are independently verified (see debt-service-spec.json's engine-limitation notes) to ALREADY equal the facility's own true contractual amounts to the penny every month checked, because Selvara carries no debt other than this one facility (no sweep-in risk the ledger-vs-contract distinction usually guards against). The generated debt-service-schedule.json, by contrast, is only an APPROXIMATION of the true contract (engine v1 cannot model the agreement's declining-balance amortization base or its apparent flat/30-360-style interest convention -- see debt-service-spec.json ambiguities). Sign-off should confirm whether Fixed_Charges' cash-interest/principal components should bind to the generated (approximate) covenant-support rows as specified here, or directly to the borrower's own native 'Cash interest' / 'Required principal' lines, which for this borrower are the more precise source.

measurement_window_correction_history.what_happened: At BOTH the 2026-03-31 and 2026-06-30 quarterly Test Dates, Selvara's compliance team originally computed and submitted FCCR using a SINGLE MONTH of Covenant EBITDA and fixed charges instead of the agreement's TRAILING TWELVE MONTHS (the agreement states the FCCR is a trailing-twelve-month ratio -- see this covenant's own agreement_ref and the FIXED CHARGE COVERAGE RATIO clause). The lender queried both submissions (March_Lender_TTM_Query.pdf, 2026-04-16; June_Lender_TTM_Query.pdf, 2026-07-17), directing the borrower to 'preserve the original certificate, deliver a corrected TTM workbook, and do not describe a breach as cured.' Corrected TTM figures were then issued: March 1.0338x (originally submitted in error as 0.8350x) and June 0.9192x (originally submitted in error as 0.9133x). BOTH the erroneous single-month figures and the corrected TTM figures are breaches of the 1.2000x minimum -- the correction changed the MEASURED MAGNITUDE, not the compliance VERDICT.
measurement_window_correction_history.why_it_matters_for_this_spec: This covenant's own 'window' field above is explicitly set to 'ttm' (NOT 'spot' or a monthly window) precisely because of this history -- a monitoring run that read this covenant on a single-month window would reproduce the same measurement-window error the borrower's own compliance team made twice in a row. Use ONLY the corrected TTM figures for cross-checking March and June 2026 (see cert_ref).
measurement_window_correction_history.process_signal: The SAME single-month-vs-TTM mistake recurring in two consecutive quarters is itself a controls/process signal for the analyst's broader credit view, independent of the covenant math itself.

decisions.question: Should Fixed_Charges' cash-interest and scheduled-principal components bind to the generated (approximate) debt-service-schedule rows, or directly to this borrower's own native 'Cash interest' / 'Required principal' Cash-Flow-tab lines, which are independently verified exact (Selvara carries no other debt to create a ledger-vs-contract gap)?
options_considered: Accept as parsed: bind to the generated covenant-support rows per the standard template convention
Bind directly to the native ledger lines, since they are demonstrably more precise for this specific borrower
decisions.decision: Bind Fixed_Charges' cash_interest and scheduled_principal components directly to the borrower's own native 'Cash interest' and 'Required principal' Cash-Flow-tab lines, NOT the generated debt-service-schedule.
decisions.rationale: This is the highest-stakes covenant in the whole 6-borrower onboarding batch: two consecutive breaches, an expired waiver, and a test date 15 days away. The generated schedule is a known, quantified approximation (flat-original-principal amortization base vs. the agreement's declining-balance reality; a flat 30/360-style interest convention the engine can't reproduce -- see debt-service-spec.json), while the native ledger lines are independently verified exact to the penny in every month checked. Using the less precise source on the covenant closest to an active breach is not defensible when a verified, more precise source is directly available. build-monitoring-model should populate the covenant-support rows from the native ledger for this borrower, not the generated schedule.

decisions.question: No executed document states a cash interest rate, index, margin, or day-count. Accept the reverse-engineered flat ~10.2551% rate (derived from the borrower's own books, consistent to 9-10 significant figures across 17 non-adjacent months)?
options_considered: Accept as parsed: use the reverse-engineered rate as the best-available reading, clearly flagged as an assumption
Leave the rate entirely unset and refuse to model cash interest at all
decisions.decision: Accept as parsed. The reverse-engineered rate stands as an assumption, but per the fixed_charges_component_source decision above, the covenant test itself reads the native ledger directly, so this ambiguity no longer propagates into the live FCCR test -- only into the informational debt-service-schedule.json output.
decisions.rationale: The rate's precision matters far less now that Fixed_Charges reads the native ledger. Recommend confirming against a longer-form agreement if one is ever located, since the reviewed original_agreement.pdf reads as a one-page excerpt missing an interest-rate section entirely.

decisions.question: Accept the engine's flat, original-principal-base amortization and its non-matching interest day-count, now that both are informational only?
options_considered: Accept as parsed: keep the generated schedule as a documented approximation for informational/forward-looking purposes only
Suppress the generated schedule entirely given it does not tie
decisions.decision: Accept as parsed: keep the generated schedule, clearly labeled as an approximation not used for the live covenant test.
decisions.rationale: Same engine-limitation class already documented for Nemeris, Orinth Vale, and Asteron. Removing the schedule entirely would lose a useful (if imprecise) forward reference; the real risk would be treating it as authoritative, which it is not, here.

decisions.question: The 2025-Q1 (2025-03-31) TTM Build spans back to 2024-04, five months before the borrower's earliest monthly package and nine months before the 2025-01-15 closing, on an apparent pro-forma basis the agreement's text does not describe.
options_considered: Accept as parsed: record as a flagged ambiguity, use the certified 2025-03-31 figure as reported without attempting to independently reconstruct the pre-close pro-forma convention
Reject the 2025-03-31 test date as not evaluable given the undocumented convention
decisions.decision: Accept as parsed. The certified 2025-03-31 figure (1.6245x, compliant) stands as reported for the historical trend line. The model side of covenant-compliance will independently read 'insufficient history' for that date once build-monitoring-model runs, since the model only goes back to the borrower's earliest monthly package -- that is the correct, honest outcome rather than fabricating a reconstruction of an undocumented pro-forma convention.
decisions.rationale: This date is not the borrower's live problem (it was comfortably compliant); worth flagging for completeness but not worth blocking anything today.

decisions.question: The security agreement never states 'first priority' verbatim -- is the inferred first-priority reading (from the facility's own naming and the closing mechanics extinguishing prior liens) acceptable?
options_considered: Accept as parsed: first-priority is the best-supported reading
decisions.rationale: Standard, sufficient evidence for a first-priority reading in a refinancing context; no competing lien is disclosed anywhere in the documents reviewed.
